Perfect! After **axb6**, White captures the loose pawn, advances to promotion, and wins. Black cannot prevent the queen promotion. The main line is:

**axb6** (capturing the loose pawn) → Black tries **e3** → **b7** → Black tries **e2** → **b8=Q** and White has a queen.

This wins because after capturing the undefended b6 pawn, White's passed pawn on the 6th rank will reach promotion while Black's e-pawn can't deliver a queen.

---

**Coaching Note:**

When you can capture an undefended pawn, check if it gives you a dangerous passed pawn. Here, axb6 removes Black's defender and pushes White's pawn deep into the board. With your king supporting nearby and Black's king out of range, the passed pawn will queen before Black's e-pawn can. Always calculate whether the resulting position is a win, not just whether the capture is safe.
